title: Separable residue field: the cotangent space injects into the differentials
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a $k$-algebra, with residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, a field extension of $k$ via $k\to R\to\kappa$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume $\kappa$ is finitely generated as a field over $k$ ($\kappa=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_i\in\kappa$) and separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Let $\Omega_{R/k}$ and $\mathrm d:R\to\Omega_{R/k}$ be the module of Kähler differentials and the universal derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then the $\kappa$-linear map $$\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\longrightarrow\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa,\qquad a\bmod\mathfrak m^2\longmapsto\mathrm da\otimes1\quad(a\in\mathfrak m),$$ is injective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TU (lemma-computation-differential, line 38687), proof lines 38702-38737; tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00TU,algebra-lemma-computation-differential)

proof.text: Put $A=R/\mathfrak m^2$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\subset A$, and let $q:A\to\kappa$ be the residue map. Then $\mathfrak n^2=0$ and $A/\mathfrak n=\kappa$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-mod-power-ideal] with $S=R$, $I=\mathfrak m$, and $n=1$, the quotient $R\to A$ induces an isomorphism $\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa$ taking $\mathrm da\otimes1$ to $\mathrm d\bar a\otimes1$. The quotient map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\mathfrak n$ is the identity on residue classes. Thus it suffices to prove injectivity of $\mathfrak n\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\kappa$, $u\mapsto\mathrm du\otimes1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TU (lemma-computation-differential), lines 38702-38704; differential comparison is Lemma Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal) with n=1

proof.text: Since $\kappa/k$ is finitely generated and separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], choose a separating transcendence basis $\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. It is finite: if $\kappa=k(a_1,\ldots,a_N)$, algebraic independence forces $r\le N$, and $\kappa$ is algebraic and generated as a field by the finitely many $a_j$ over $F=k(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r)$, hence finite over $F$. This finite algebraic extension is separable by the choice of basis [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-primitive-element], choose $\bar y\in\kappa$ with $\kappa=F(\bar y)$. Its monic minimal polynomial $P\in F[T]$ is separable, so $P(\bar y)=0$ and $P'(\bar y)\ne0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TU (lemma-computation-differential), lines 38704-38714; finite separable primitive element is Fields Lemma Tag 030N

proof.text: Lift each $\bar x_i$ to $x_i\in A$. Algebraic independence says that every nonzero polynomial $f\in k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$ has $f(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r)\ne0$ in $\kappa$. Hence $f(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ lies outside the maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of the local ring $A$ and is a unit: if it were a nonunit, its principal ideal would lie in a maximal ideal, necessarily $\mathfrak n$. The evaluation map $k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to A$ therefore extends uniquely by fractions to a $k$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:F=k(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r)\to A$ whose composite with $q$ is the inclusion $F\hookrightarrow\kappa$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TU (lemma-computation-differential), lines 38714-38721 (the displayed commutative triangle)

proof.text: Choose any $y_0\in A$ with $q(y_0)=\bar y$ and evaluate the polynomial $P^\varphi\in A[T]$ obtained by applying $\varphi$ to its coefficients. Since $P(\bar y)=0$, $c=P^\varphi(y_0)$ lies in $\mathfrak n$. Since $P'(\bar y)\ne0$, $u=(P')^\varphi(y_0)$ has nonzero residue and is a unit of $A$ by the local-ring argument of step 3. Put $\delta=-u^{-1}c\in\mathfrak n$ and $y=y_0+\delta$. As $\mathfrak n^2=0$, polynomial expansion gives $P^\varphi(y)=P^\varphi(y_0)+(P')^\varphi(y_0)\delta=c-u u^{-1}c=0$. Thus evaluation $T\mapsto y$ defines an $F$-algebra homomorphism $F[T]/(P)\to A$. The natural $F$-algebra isomorphism $F[T]/(P)\cong F(\bar y)=\kappa$ makes this a $k$-algebra section $\sigma:\kappa\to A$ of $q$: on $F$ its residue is the inclusion by step 3, and it sends $\bar y$ to $y$ with residue $\bar y$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TU (lemma-computation-differential), lines 38721-38734 (simple-root adjustment in the square-zero ideal)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-square-zero-section-conormal-retraction] to the surjective $k$-algebra map $q:A\to\kappa$, its square-zero kernel $\mathfrak n$, and the section $\sigma$ of step 4. It gives a left inverse to $\mathfrak n\to\kappa\otimes_A\Omega_{A/k}$, $u\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm du$, hence this map is injective. The symmetry of the tensor product identifies this map with $u\mapsto\mathrm du\otimes1$ in step 1, and step 1's differential isomorphism identifies that map with the map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R\kappa$ in the statement. Therefore the latter is injective.
